summary: Andreas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied under traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Spengel (1838–1905) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1856–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1860–1862), and later taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies. Messent earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams, also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrei Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) and later taught Bidia Dandaron.
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett (born 1961) works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (~1983–1990) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1995).

Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA, and PhD under Richard G. Salomon), also studying under Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.

Andrew Goudie (born 1945) is a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Dean Close School (~1958–1963) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1964–1970), and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (1970–2014).

Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Sri Narayana Mishra and served as Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew Ollett (born 1986) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (~2006–2008) and Columbia University (~2009–2016), and became an associate professor at the University of Chicago (~2020).

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University, with teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler (born 1941) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard (~1958–1962) and Yale (~1962–1967) under Warren Crawford Cowgill, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1967–1999).

Andrew Watsky (born 1957) works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1987–1994), taught Bryan D. Lowe, and held a post at Vassar College (~1994–2008).
Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, held posts at Hamburg (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2018–2021), and taught Kenji Takahashi.

Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy (~1970–1975), taught Ming Mei, and held a post at the Museum of history of religion (~1978–1992).

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig. He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and Lviv (1917) and founded Rocznik Orientalistyczny, among other societies.

András Róna-Tas (born 1931) works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and held posts at Szeged (1968–2002), Vienna, SCAS, and the IATS.
